title: Telus says 'small number' of calls interrupted in Eastern Canada on Thursday
summary: An outage map on the Telus website showed issues with phone and wireless services in several provinces on Thursday.

image.caption: Telus's headquarters in downtown Vancouver is seen on May 6. The company reported mobile and wireless service outages affecting parts of Ontario, Quebec, B.C. and Alberta on Thursday, some of which have since been resolved. (Ben Nelms/CBC)

blocks.text: An outage map on the Telus website showed issues with phone and wireless services in several provinces on Thursday.
Customers in Western Canada not affected by the same service disruptions reported Thursday
An outage was reported at around 9:40 a.m. ET on Thursday in southwestern Ontario, according to the company's website.

"Services are currently experiencing a disruption impacting mobile devices, which may affect your ability to reach emergency [911] services," Telus said, which also noted that there is "911 wireless fallback coverage provided by an alternate carrier in this region."
The Windsor Police Service said the outage had caused intermittent issues with its non-emergency line, but that Windsor's emergency line remains unaffected.
In a statement to CBC News, a Telus spokesperson said a "small number" of calls in Eastern Canada reported service interruptions Thursday morning.
"All services have been restored, and calls to emergency 911 services remained fully operational," the statement said.

items: 911 services fully restored after outages affect Ontario, Quebec, 4 other provinces: Bell Canada
3 major outages renew concerns about northwest B.C.'s communications network

blocks.text: In eastern Ontario, near the Ottawa area, Telus reported an interruption resulting in outbound call failures to landlines that began around 9:14 a.m. ET on Thursday. The outage appeared to be resolved after 1 p.m.
Earlier, an outage linked to a damaged cable was reported in parts of Quebec, but it appears to have since been restored.

Telus said customers in Western Canada were not affected by the same service disruptions reported Thursday, though a number of outages appeared to be ongoing in B.C. and Alberta, on the company's website.
